- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially sentiment > 0.6) — model tends to overshoot in bullish phases.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or negative (sentiment < 0.3) — model underreacts to bearish signals.
- Lag in price correction: model often delays downward revisions after recent highs, especially if sentiment is high.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent trends and fails to revert to historical mean when sentiment shifts.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early periods (e.g., 1–3 days) when sentiment is rising, then overcorrect later.
- Avoid “peak chasing” — if sentiment peaks and price spikes, model often forecasts higher than true peak, then overcorrects too aggressively.
- Use sentiment as a filter: if sentiment > 0.7, reduce forecast slope; if sentiment < 0.3, increase downward bias.
